_help: [NOT WIRED YET] Design 5 Oct §EK (the whole animal). A hunter's kill goes in the workshop hut door (camps.json sim.hunt) and is never seen cut; after process_game_h the animal comes out as pieces on their stations. Keyed by the creature catalogue's size class and kind, never per species (a people file's dressing and the biome do the rest). Each part says which bench it goes to (soft, hard, hearth, kiln: camps.json sim.workshop.benches) and the piece that appears (a camps.json store.pieces vocabulary row, one visible object). food: the units added to the food store (sim.hunt.food_units has the number). never: nothing from any creature goes to a weapon that touches what lurks in the dark (§ED.7): bowstrings and fletching are for hunting. The reverence is in the use: one creature visibly becomes several needful things, and nothing says so. Real analogues cited at the bottom as elsewhere (§BO). First guesses; the designer owns them.

hide.note: brain-tanned: every animal has just enough brain to tan its own hide

becomes: a skin bag with the down in
a dried oily fish burned as a candle (the candlefish)
the stone lamp: light and heat and the cooking fire of a people with no trees (§BP, the tundra's light)

pieces_vocabulary.hide_on_frame: a hide laced into a pole frame by the soft bench, hair side out, then flesh side; two frames at most
pieces_vocabulary.pelt_on_stretcher: a small pelt on a forked stick, a row of them under the eave
pieces_vocabulary.sinew_hank: a hank of pale sinew hung from a peg
pieces_vocabulary.gut_drying: a loop of gut over a pole
pieces_vocabulary.feather_bundle: a bundle of feathers tied at the quill, hung
pieces_vocabulary.fish_skin_drying: fish skins pegged flat on a board
pieces_vocabulary.bone_tools_in_row: awls, needles and a scraper laid in a row on the hard bench, more as the camp hunts
pieces_vocabulary.antler_haft: an antler with a flint set in it, leaning
pieces_vocabulary.horn_cup: a horn cup on the bench edge
pieces_vocabulary.tooth_pendant: a tooth on a cord, hung by the door
pieces_vocabulary.big_bones_stacked: rib and jaw stacked like timber
pieces_vocabulary.shell_bowl: a turtle shell as a bowl, upturned to dry
pieces_vocabulary.glue_pot: a small pot of hoof glue warming by the fire
pieces_vocabulary.meat_strips_on_rack: thin strips over the rack (camps.json food_pieces)
pieces_vocabulary.spit_over_fire: a small animal on a spit
pieces_vocabulary.fish_on_rack: fish hung on the drying rack (camps.json food_pieces)
pieces_vocabulary.eggs_in_basket: eggs in a basket by the store
pieces_vocabulary.rendering_pot: a pot of fat on a hearth stone, a skin on it; the lamp is filled from it
pieces_vocabulary.cracked_bones_by_fire: long bones split beside the hearth
pieces_vocabulary.stone_lamp_burning: a stone bowl of oil with a moss wick, lit day and night in the hut doorway (the only warm light in a treeless camp)
pieces_vocabulary.dung_cake: dung cakes drying in a row (camps.json wood_piece_by_fuel)

never: a weapon that touches what lurks in the dark (§ED.7)
a hunter shown handing out his own kill (§EJ.2)

real_world.note: hide for tipi covers, robes and parfleche; bone awls, scrapers and shoulder-blade hoes; sinew thread and bowstrings; horn cups and spoons; brain tanning; pemmican of pounded dried meat, fat and berries that kept for years; dried dung as fuel on treeless plains
the Inuit soapstone lamp burning seal or whale blubber with a moss or cottongrass wick: the only light, heat and cooking fire in a snow house
a Pacific smelt so oily that a dried one with a wick through it burns as a candle; its grease was a trade good along the grease trails
Nivkh, Ainu, Nanai and Alaskan Yup'ik fish-skin boots, bags and coats; salmon skin tanned and sewn with sinew
the animal's own brain emulsified in water dresses its hide; smoked afterwards so it stays soft when wet
